To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“The inhibition of Rac1 signaling sensitized lung carcinoma cells to TNF-mediated cell death.”

the expression of dominant negative mutants of IKKβ and Rac1 in A549 cells sensitizes these lung cancer cells to apoptosis induced by exposure to TNFα, whereas the expression of a constitutively active Rac1 mutant (V12Rac1), which mimics the activated form of Rac1, protects A549 cells against TNFα-induced cytotoxicity.
the inhibition of both the Rac1 and IKB kinase (IKK) signaling pathways in A549 human lung adenocarcinoma cells sensitizes the cells to tumor necrosis factor (TNF) α-induced cell death.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of TNFα signaling in lung carcinoma.
the molecular and cellular mechanisms of tumor cell death.
the role of NF-κB in the regulation of apoptosis and the mechanisms of NF-κ B activation in lung cancer cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TNFα-induced lung carcinoma cell apoptosis is mediated through a Rac1-dependent IKK pathway.
concurrent inhibition of the Rac1 and IKB kinase pathways sensitizes lung carcinoma cells to TNF-α-induced apoptosis.
the expression of dominant negative IKK and Rac1 sensitizes A549 cells to TNF-α-induced apoptosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the combination of Rac1 dominant negative mutant (N17Rac1), IKKβ dominant positive mutant (IKKβKA), and TNFα treatment results in apoptosis in lung cancer cells, and this effect is mediated through NF-κB.
we have shown that inhibition of both IKK and Rac pathways sensitizes lung tumor cells to TNF-induced apoptosis.
the expression of a dominant negative mutant to IKKβ (IKKβKA), a critical regulator of the transcription factor, NF-κB, sensitized lung cancer cells to the cytotoxic effects of TNFα.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified two key proteins, IKK and Rac1, that can be targeted in combination to sensitize lung cancer cells to the cytotoxic effects of TNFalpha.
we have found a new way to make cancer cells more sensitive to a drug that is already in the clinic.
the inhibition of two signaling pathways, the Rac1 and NF-κβ pathways, can sensitize lung cancer cells to the apoptotic effects of TNF-α.
